title: Email — SMTP/POP3/IMAP
html:
Three protocols, three different jobs in the lifecycle of an email.

Sending — SMTP

Definition

SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is the application-layer protocol used to send email between mail servers, running over TCP so no data is lost in transit.

Sender
→
Sender's SMTP server
→
Receiver's SMTP server
→
Receiver

To find which server handles mail for a domain, a special DNS record is queried — the MX (Mail Exchange) record, checkable via dig -type=mx gmail.com.

Receiving (download & delete) — POP3

Definition

POP3 (Post Office Protocol v3) runs on port 110. The client authenticates with the POP server, downloads all mail to the local device, then typically deletes it from the server, and closes the session.

Limitation: because mail is downloaded and removed, POP3 doesn't sync well across multiple devices — your inbox on your phone and laptop can end up out of sync.

Receiving (multi-device sync) — IMAP

Definition

IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) allows your email to remain on the server and stay synced across multiple devices — instead of downloading and deleting, it mirrors the server-side state on every device.
